title: Relationships among Inflammatory Biomarkers and Self-Reported Treatment-Related Symptoms in Patients Treated with Chemotherapy for Gynecologic Cancer: A Controlled Comparison
notes: NO COGNITIVE OUTCOMES MEASURED — paper assesses fatigue, depression, sleep, physical activity only. Uses random-effects fluctuation mixed models. Actual parameter estimates in Supplementary Table S3 (not in PDF). Key qualitative findings: between-person CRP→depression (p=0.01); within-person CRP→physical_activity (p=0.03). No significant effects for IL-6, TNF-alpha on fatigue or sleep. Cancer type: gynecologic (ovarian/endometrial/cervical). 5 timepoints: pre-chemo1, pre-chemo3, pre-chemo6, 6mo post, 12mo post. Biomarkers: TNF-alpha, TNFR1, TNFR2, IL-6, IL-10, IL-1b, IL-1ra, CRP.
extraction_status: NO_EDGE_EVIDENCE — no cognitive outcomes, effect sizes in supplementary materials

qualitative_findings.CRP_depression: Between-person CRP associated with greater depression (p=0.01), main effect across patients and controls
qualitative_findings.CRP_physical_activity: Within-person CRP fluctuations associated with less physical activity (p=0.03), main effect
qualitative_findings.null_fatigue: No inflammatory biomarker associated with fatigue
qualitative_findings.null_sleep: No inflammatory biomarker associated with sleep disturbance
qualitative_findings.null_group_interaction: CRP-symptom associations not stronger for cancer patients than controls
